This is a logical and necessary adjustment for this specific image instance. The testable checkpoints regarding rind color, flesh translucency, and seed cavity structure were marked present, which aligns with visual evidence. I agree with all verdicts.
artifact_review: The Router flagged a texture anomaly on the background fruit (severity 2) and slight boundary fusion in the background peppers (severity 1). The Perceptual Quality Auditor found no graphics-level distortions (noise/blur), which supports the high clarity of the main subject. However, the Topology Boundary Auditor's mask (showing only one slice isolated) confirms the main subject is structurally sound, but does not rule out the background fusion noted by the Router. The 'plastic' look of the background fruit is a valid minor artifact. I agree with the severity ratings; they are minor and do not detract significantly from the primary subject's realism.
alignment_reasoning: The fine-grained classifier strongly confirms the class as 'cucumber' (logit 8.16 vs 5.0 for zucchini), distinguishing it from look-alikes. All biologically relevant visible features (rind, flesh, seeds) match the taxonomy perfectly. The inability to check global shape is due to cropping/slicing, not generation failure. High alignment score reflects perfect conformance of visible parts.
artifact_reasoning: The primary subject (cucumber slices) shows zero structural artifacts. The background contains minor issues: slight fusion between red peppers/tomatoes and an overly smooth/plastic texture on the upper-right fruit. These are low-severity artifacts typical of AI-generated complex scenes but do not compromise the integrity of the target class. The perceptual auditor found no noise or blur, supporting a high artifact score despite the minor background issues.
